title: Domains and Ranges of Sum and Product Functions
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Given the real-valued functions f(x) = x and g(x) = sqrt(x - 1), determine the natural domains and ranges of f, g, the sum f + g, and the product f * g.
finalAnswer: D_f = (-\infty, \infty),\ R_f = (-\infty, \infty);\quad D_g = [1, \infty),\ R_g = [0, \infty);\quad D_{f+g} = [1, \infty),\ R_{f+g} = [1, \infty);\quad D_{f\cdot g} = [1, \infty),\ R_{f\cdot g} = [0, \infty)

steps.title: Determine the Domain and Range of Each Component Function
steps.explanation: The identity function f(x) = x is defined for all real numbers and takes every real value as an output. For g(x) = sqrt(x - 1), the radicand must be non-negative (x - 1 >= 0), giving x >= 1, and the principal square root yields all non-negative real numbers.
steps.why: Even-indexed radicals require non-negative radicands in the real number system, and the principal square root is non-negative and surjective onto [0, infinity).

steps.title: Find the Domains of f + g and f * g
steps.explanation: Both the sum (f + g)(x) = x + sqrt(x - 1) and the product (f * g)(x) = x * sqrt(x - 1) are defined wherever both f(x) and g(x) are simultaneously defined, which is the intersection of their individual domains.
steps.why: The domain of an algebraic sum or product of two functions is the intersection of their natural domains.

steps.title: Determine the Range of the Sum f + g
steps.explanation: On [1, infinity), both x and sqrt(x - 1) are continuous and strictly increasing. At the left endpoint x = 1, (f + g)(1) = 1 + 0 = 1, and as x -> infinity, x + sqrt(x - 1) -> infinity, so the range is [1, infinity).
steps.why: The sum of two continuous increasing functions on [1, infinity) is continuous and increasing, mapping [1, infinity) onto [(f+g)(1), infinity).

steps.title: Determine the Range of the Product f * g
steps.explanation: On [1, infinity), both factors x > 0 and sqrt(x - 1) >= 0 are continuous, non-negative, and increasing. At x = 1, (f * g)(1) = 1 * 0 = 0, and as x -> infinity, x * sqrt(x - 1) grows without bound, yielding the range [0, infinity).
steps.why: The product of two non-negative continuous increasing functions on [1, infinity) is continuous and increasing from its minimum value at x = 1 to infinity.
